prompt: make the bouncer tests pass on linux too
result:
The bouncer tests now pass on Linux. There's no separate bouncer plugin: the bouncer is part of `bws-enhance`. All 54 of its tests pass with `claude plugin test` (before the fix, 4 failed), and `claude plugin validate` passes. I couldn't run the full gate, because tsc won't run here (details below).

**Cause:** the tests use a Windows project root, `C:/proj`. Linux doesn't treat that as an absolute path, so the engine joined it onto the current folder before handing it to the test's file stubs. The stubs got paths like `…/bws-enhance/C:/proj/AGENTS.md`, found nothing, and behaved as if the glossary and instruction files didn't exist. That broke three bouncer glossary tests and one `/enhance` test in `enhance.test.ts` with the same cause, so I fixed both files.

**Fix:** only the tests changed. The `fs.read` and `fs.list` stubs in `bws-enhance/tests/bounce.test.ts` and `bws-enhance/tests/enhance.test.ts` now drop everything before the drive letter, with a one-line comment saying why. On Windows the paths have no such prefix, so nothing changes there, but I haven't run the tests on Windows.

**Why tsc didn't run:**
- `tools/mods-gate.py` has tsc's location hardcoded to a Windows path. You can override it with the `MODS_TSC` environment variable, but that alone wasn't enough.
- The generated `.claude-plugin/types/` folder doesn't exist in this worktree, and there's no copy anywhere on this machine. Neither `claude plugin test`, `plugin validate` nor a headless `--plugin-dir` run created it, so tsc can't find `claude-code`.
- I installed tsc 5.8.3 in the scratchpad (`/tmp/claude-0/-tmp-claude-0--home-user-bws-claude-mods-dev-760f7ba1-34a3-5ceb-b711-31332de7c2eb-scratchpad-wt-linux-tests--raw--opus/dfef2b21-aaa5-416a-ba53-2f4c104dcf08/scratchpad/ts`), but without the types it has nothing to check against. To type-check, run the gate on Windows, or here once the types exist, with `MODS_TSC` pointing at that tsc.

The change is test-only, so there's no version bump or release. I haven't committed it and didn't add a `runs/` entry; say if you want either.
